Title: THE PROVISION OF TUBERCULOSIS TESTING USING THE TB SPOT TB ASSAY FOR ARMY RECRUITS
Description:
1.The Ministry of Defence (MOD) ("the Authority") recruits approximately 400 Gurkha 
soldiers into the British Army each year.
2.Upon arrival in the UK, to begin training as British soldiers the recruits undergo health 
immigration screening which due to their origin in Nepal needs to include screening 
for Latent Tuberculosis Infection (LTBI).
REQUIREMENT
3.The requirement is for the provision of Tuberculosis (TB) testing using the T SPOT®.TB assay. 
4. The number of tests required will be approximately 400 Gurkha and 1280 Foreign and 
Commonwealth recruits per annum. Initial testing is anticipated to commence in Jan 23 and 
will be repeated annually thereafter until the end of the contract.
4.Research shows that the initial test may be obscured by presence of other conditions 
which may affect up to approximately 25% of the recruit population. Individuals 
where this may be the case will require to be retested subsequent to treatment of 
their conditions. The Authority therefore requires this contract to cover the retesting 
of a subset of the recruit population estimated at up to 70 individuals, at a later date 
to be agreed between the Designated Officer and the Contractor. 
5.The Authority will contact the contractor and inform them of the dates of the Intake and 
how many recruits they are expecting.

Title: PROVISION OF HELMINTH SCREENING TESTING, FOR ARMY RECRUITS AT INFANTRY TRAINING CENTRE (ITC) CATTERICK MEDICAL CENTRE
Description:
The Ministry of Defence (MOD) recruits approximately 400 Gurkha Soldiers into the British Army each year. 

 

Upon arrival in the UK, the recruits undergo health screening, helminths/parasite infections including strongyloides. 

 
Research has shown that the presence of helminths infection (present in approximately 25% of recruits) was associated with a false negative Interferon Gamma Release Assay (IGRA) test and recommended that those who had a helminths infection should have their IGRA test repeated after treatment to exclude Latent Tuberculosis Infection (LTBI).  The implications are that a small proportion of those who are incorrectly diagnosed will go on to develop active Tuberculosis (TB). 

 

This requirement is for the provision Helminths Screening Testing Services for the Gurkha recruitment intake of approximately 400 personnel annually for the length of the contract. 

The Contractor will provide the stool specimen pots and serology tubes for each recruit plus an extra 10% in case of repeats/breakages.  These should arrive at the Authority's premises at the Initial Training Centre (ITC) Catterick. For the Gurkha recruitment intake of approximately 400 personnel the MOD requires: 

 

Stool Concentration Culture (1 x test for each Patient) 

 

Stool Culture (1 x test for each patient) 

 

Stool PCR (1 x test for each patient) 

 

Strongyloides Elisa Antibody Test and frozen serum store (1 x test for each patient)

Title: The Provision of Yoga at Defence Medical Rehabilitation Centre Stanford Hall
Description: 1.Yoga has been a key component of patient physical and psychological recovery at the Defence Medical Rehabilitation Centre (DMRC) Headley Court and now at DMRC StanfordHall (SH) since 2012. It has proven to be a highly beneficial component of the rehabilitation offered to military patients 2. Evidence from published research demonstrate that yoga is effective at improving a variety of health-related outcome measures. In addition, there is proven benefit for the management of mental health concerns including stress, anger management, sleep and mood issues which is key in the bio-psychosocial management approach offered by DMRC. 3. Recent anecdotal evidence collected from patients indicated that the yoga sessions provided are highly regarded and contribute immensely to overall patient morale, whilst significantly improving their rehabilitation journey.  4. The Authority will require a Contractor to provide yoga sessions to a wide variety of patients at DMRC SH.  5.The requirement is the delivery of:a.8 x 1-Hour sessions each week that are adaptable to cater for the individual needs of the patients receiving in-patient provision from Upper Quadrant Rehab, Specialisation Rehab, Complex Trauma Rehab, Neurological Rehab, Spines Rehab, Lower Limb Rehab, Mild Traumatic Brain Injury and Vestibular Rehab., b.5 Extra classes every three months for Mild traumatic brain injury(mTBI)and Vestibular Rehab (2 classes for mTBI and 3 classes for Vestibular Rehab) 6.The Contractor is required to record participation levels for each yoga session and forward a monthly summary to the Designated Officer (DO) for audit purposes.7.The Contractor shall liaise with a member of DMRC rehabilitation staff prior to each yoga sessions in order to receive a verbal brief of patient conditions and identify any individual patient considerations/adaptations. The Contractor is never to go against any clinical direction provided by DMRC rehabilitation staff.8.The Contractor shall be required to produce an effective Yoga Session Plan unique to different patient populations taking into account health and safety considerations. All patient safety incidents are to be reported to the DO within 24 hours.The Contractor is to provide evidence of an effective Business Continuity Plan to provide alternate staff to deliver sessions to ensure session delivery is not interrupted by more than 24 hours

Title: 705490450 - Supply of Digital Optical Micrometers
Description:
Awarded Contract 
Supply of Digital Optical Micrometers
The Authority has a requirement to procure Digital Optical Micrometers.
The 8400K Digital Optical Micrometer is mandated for use on aircraft and aircraft equipment across the Defence Air Environment for the inspection of windows and canopies in accordance with OEM and NAVAIR Systems Command and Air Publication documentation for the Digital Optical Micrometer 8400K.

Optical micrometers are used to measure and evaluate the width or depth of scratches, cracks, pits, corrosion, dents and other blemishes in a variety of materials. They can also be used to quantify the height of spurs and other small protrusions. For transparent materials, this instrument is useful for measuring thickness, depth of crazing, depth of fractures, and width of embedded voids. Changes to the capability definition may occur periodically as Defence and/or foreign policy is revised in response to shifts in the global geo-political situation.

The optical micrometer allows "repair or replace" maintenance decisions to be made with absolute certainty. The approved in-service Digital Optical Micrometer is the 8400K Digital Optical Micrometer, Nato Stock Number: 6650-01-220-8942.

In the unlikely event support services are required in the future by the authority they will be requested separately.

In March 2020, the Prime Minister called on manufacturers to help the UK to step up production of ventilators to support the UK's response to the virus and save lives. This included working on new or adapted ventilator designs, as well the Government's work to buy ventilators from abroad.

A contract award Notice was published on 25 May 2020 (reference 2020/S 100-243206) covering contracts awarded pursuant to the RMVS programme. This is a second contract award notice that covers contracts awarded thereafter.

Additional Text:
This contract was awarded as a result of the RMVS project.

RMVS CANs

Existing CANs relating to the RMVS project are 2020/S 100-243206, 2020/S 167-406004 and 2021/S 002-003456 (RMVS CANs).

Due to the need to respond rapidly to the emerging situation, some design work, testing, developing and manufacturing was undertaken before a formalised contract with known costs and outputs was put in place between Cabinet Office and those RMVS suppliers at the time of the RMVS CANs.

Instead Cabinet Office gave commitments to those RMVS suppliers to enable those suppliers to support the RMVS project at significant pace and to mitigate those suppliers operating entirely at risk during extremely turbulent and changing circumstances. The RMVS CANs reflected the estimated values as best known at the time and cost caps within which suppliers were operating.

At the time of the RMVS CANs, in order to be as transparent as possible with the market, information available at the time of entering into those commitments was provided, notwithstanding that it was expected to take several months to settle on the final output and resulting contracts.

The RMVS CANs were therefore published to notify the market of the estimated and maximum limits of the commitments Cabinet Office had entered into to support the RMVS project. Where a supplier appears on more than one RMVS CAN, this reflects an increase to the estimate or cost cap previously notified to the market.

Title: LogFAS Enablement Scoping Study
Description:
CDS via VCDS has directed DCDS (MilCap) and CDLS to continue to exploit the Performance Excellence regime implemented by CDLS and the FLC 2* support champions.

There is recognition and a mandate to move faster, and we need to make sure that the full range of opportunities for improving availability are examined.  This means thinking beyond logistic and equipment support.  MOD must identify the opportunities that will come from addressing the full range of DLOD constraints as well as policies, permissions, and authorities where these are material. 

Support needs to be provided to the Commands in prioritising work to ensure that we focus scarce resources on the most important challenges and biggest opportunities.  We must aim to deliver a year-on-year incremental improvement in the outputs from Defence.  Accordingly, the Increasing Defence Outputs project has been established to Set the Conditions for Defence to Deliver Against CDS Ambition, and will:

•	Develop a Defence Performance Framework within which single services can drive forward increased outputs.
•	Develop a cost/value of availability model and make recommendations on Decision-Support Tool functionality needed to make timely interven-tions and investments.
•	Ensure coherence across all TLB in-flight projects and address any im-pediments to unlocking greater availability by reviewing and amending relevant policies, authorities, doctrine and process. 
•	Share best practice and lessons from across Defence, international partners and industry.
•	Develop, in consultation with industry, a revised contract management model that delivers greater affordability and availability.
•	Assist single services with setting the level of ambition for year-on-year improvements, captured in Defence Plan 23, and assist with identifying ABC 23 investment opportunities.
•	Develop an initial set of principles for embedding availability targets into the acquisition process

Title: Provision of Anatomical and Simulation Facilities in support of the Defence Medical Services (DMS) delivered Military Operational Specialist Team Training (MOSTT) Course
Description:
The Authority requires surgical team training that is achieved in the main by a 5-day Military Operational Specialist Team Training (MOSTT) course. This is delivered by a military faculty comprising personnel from the Defence Medical Services (DMS).

The Tenderer is to provide facilities in support a minimum of 2 and up to a maximum of 4 MOSTT courses per annum to accommodate a maximum of 54 participants (i.e. 6 teams of 9 participants) per course.
Key areas that the Tenderer must provide:
a. Source, supply and maintain appropriate resources to deliver a training course aimed at preparing delegates to deliver military Damage Control Resuscitation and Surgery, to prepare the patient/s for critical care transportation in a deployed team.

b. Provide a Human Tissue Authority licensed surgical skills workshop facility to enable surgeons to undertake technical skills training on human cadavers.

c. Supply, prepare, maintain and dispose of up to 3 (fresh or thawed from frozen) full human cadavers in accordance with the Human Tissue Act 2004 and requirements of the UK Human Tissue Authority for 2.5 days for surgical technical skills training.

d. Supply, prepare, maintain and dispose of up to 3 (fresh or thawed from frozen) human cadaveric torsos in accordance with the Human Tissue Act 2004 and requirements of the UK Human Tissue Authority to enable technical skills training for anaesthetists and Emergency Medicine doctors in emergency thoracotomy for one half day.

e. Provide 10-20 prosected human specimens and deliver demonstrations of anatomy for non-medically qualified personnel and to deliver demonstrations of anatomy to Anaesthetists in support of Regional Anaesthesia Teaching.

f. Provide 5-10 prosected specimens and deliver demonstrations of canine anatomy for medically qualified personnel. Such specimens should facilitate the same learning and understanding as required for advanced trauma life support measures plus key surgical anatomy differences between human and canine patients for vascular access, cavity access, and haemorrhage control procedures in the chest and abdomen.

g. The Contractor should provide a prepared surgical set per cadaveric table and a further 'clean' set for the simulation sessions.

h. Provide two high-fidelity adult models for neurosurgical training simulation.

i. Provide an audio system that allows all area coverage within a tented environment through a set of strategically placed microphones which feedback to a mixing desk allowing the operator to select the best microphone and feed it through the visual system. 

j. A facility must have an appropriately sized room to erect a tent with the dimensions of 5.5 x 7.5 metres and height 3.5 metres, which is licenced for the use of cadavers for complex hybrid simulation.

Charter is currently sat on a now unsupported version of an Oracle DB. In order to successfully migrate the application from the current on-premises hosting to MODCloud as part of the DCR program, then the application and its data must be uplifted to a MS SQL DB.

Title: Provision of RAF Digital Various Radio Equipment including ancillaries and support
Description:
Provision of RAF Digital Various Radio Equipment including ancillaries and support, utilising the Direct Award process available on the CCS Networks Services 2 Framework (the Supplier has an existing Service Offering which met the needs of the customer).

The scope of this requirement is to enable the supply and support of PMR and DMR equipment and associated services to the RAF Digital on a call-off basis.  This requirement will result in a Call-Off Contract(s) for the provision of PMR/DMR services to the MoD and other third parties as agreed by Defence. The supplier of PMR/DMR services (Contractor) will provide standalone PMR/DMR systems for RAF Digital, with the capability to deliver services.

The PMR Service Offering is set to enable Defence users the ability to buy and support PMRs. The Service will offer complete and homogeneous collection of products through which authorised customers can directly purchase all their radio requirements.

The intended benefit of the Service is to reduce instance of users purchasing inferior products that may be incompatible with their existing equipment, and with less effective engineering support packages. The Service is to offer assured quality PMR products, commonality of equipment, engineering capabilities, maintenance packages including system Health Checks, safety cases, the Independent Audit of Safety Cases and innovative resolutions.

All radio equipment being provided will have to comply with as a minimum condition, the meeting of requirements of latest European Telecommunications Standards Institute (ETSI) Specifications (the latest version being ETSI EN 301 489-5 v2.2.1 as of 31 July 2019).
